ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all located on the grid points of a square grid. What is the value of $\tan C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, in the lattice $\triangle ADC$, we have $AD=2$, $DC=4$, and $\tan C= \frac{AD}{DC} = \frac{2}{4}=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC on grid paper, and all three vertices are on grid points. B and C are located on the same horizontal grid line, so the ray pointing from C to B is horizontal. A is at the upper left, C is at the lower right, and segment AC connects obliquely. If a perpendicular is drawn downward from A to the horizontal grid line passing through C, and the intersection point is denoted as D, then counting the grid squares in the figure shows that AD is 2 grid squares and DC is 4 grid squares. Reasoning: Angle C is formed by CA and the horizontal-left CB; since D is also on the same horizontal line passing through C, angle ACD is the same as angle C in triangle ABC. In right triangle ADC, relative to angle C, the opposite side is AD and the adjacent side is DC. Therefore tan C = AD / DC = 2 / 4 = 1/2.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that B and C lie on the same horizontal grid line, so ray CB is horizontal. Drop a vertical perpendicular from A to the horizontal line through C, meeting it at an unlabeled grid point D. Count grid squares in the figure: AD is 2 squares and DC is 4 squares. Since angle C in triangle ABC is the same as angle ACD in right triangle ADC, compute tan C as opposite over adjacent: AD/DC = 2/4 = 1/2.

method.method_draft: Assign coordinates using the square grid, with the horizontal line through B and C as a reference. From the image, relative to C, point A is 4 grid units to the left and 2 grid units above C. Thus the vector from C to A has horizontal change 4 and vertical change 2 in magnitude, while the other side forming angle C, namely CB, is horizontal. Therefore the tangent of the angle between CA and the horizontal ray CB equals vertical change divided by horizontal change: 2/4 = 1/2.
